injuries.longComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie emerged with a 4-57-0 line on seven targets against the Chiefs, with the targets, receptions and yards all pacing Arizona wideouts. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production moving forward.

injuries.longComment: The 27-year-old running back continues to shine, making two trips to the end zone for a second straight week and piling up at least 120 rushing yards for the third time in 2026. Hubbard is handling a bell-cow workload with no issues, and over six games since the Panthers' bye he's averaging nearly 25 touches a game while amassing 688 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns. injuries.longComment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

injuries.longComment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

injuries.longComment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

injuries.longComment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

injuries.longComment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. injuries.longComment: As the final score and Prescott's numbers indicate, the prolific passer was clicking on all cylinders right out of the gate against an overmatched Titans defense. Prescott had already helped stake the Cowboys to a 27-6 lead by halftime with eight- and 10-yard touchdown strikes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, respectively. Prescott struck again through the air in the second half with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Javonte Williams before closing out his touchdown tally with a two-yard toss to Brevyn Spann-Ford with just under five minutes remaining. Prescott added his second rushing touchdown of the campaign on a two-yard run in the latter portion of the third quarter, giving him his second straight five-TD performance. Prescott is up to 3,049 passing yards and a 25:6 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day home clash with the Eagles in Week 12.

injuries.longComment: Dobbins' opportunities have been dwindling since Week 7 against Arizona, when he dropped to 14 offensive snaps after tallying 31 the week prior. That contest against the Cardinals was when rookie Jonah Coleman returned from a four-game absence, and Coleman has since forced his way into Denver's lead-RB role with blossoming production that has included five rushing TDs over his past three games. Coleman got nearly every running-back snap for Denver on Sunday, with practice-squad elevation Cody Schrader logging just two snaps and Dobbins one. Despite Payton's proclamation that Dobbins still has a "super important" role with the team, there's little reason to expect him to be a reliable fantasy asset as long as Coleman is healthy.

injuries.longComment: Gibbs unsurprisingly had his work cut out for him against the Buccaneers' typically stingy run defense, but the Lions had the luxury of continuing to pound Gibbs into the line while protecting a second-half lead. Gibbs eventually broke through for a game-long 26-yard run and cashed in with one- and four-yard touchdown runs in the fourth quarter to help ice the victory. While Gibbs fell just short of his fifth 100-yard effort in the last six games, the 2023 first-round pick is up to 13 rushing touchdowns and is averaging 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Thanksgiving Day home showdown against the Bears.

Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

injuries.longComment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

injuries.longComment: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the green light to play versus the Ravens, he may be part of a timeshare in the backfield or be forced to settle for No. 2 duties behind David Montgomery (groin), who returned from a four-game absence in Week 11 to run for a season-high 107 yards.

injuries.longComment: Steichen rebuffed a report Sunday from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, who relayed that the Colts were planning to "exercise great caution" by holding Pierce out for the season as he works his way back from an aggravation of his surgically repaired heel. However, given the 3-8 Colts' place in the standings in addition to their $114 million investment in Pierce, Steichen acknowledged that the 26-year-old wideout still faces an uphill battle to make it back from IR before season's end if he's anything less than 100 percent. According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen said that Pierce currently is "doing plyometrics" and "running" after landing on IR on Sept. 26, but it's unclear how close Pierce may be to practicing.

injuries.longComment: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.longComment: Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.longComment: Lawrence just managed to generate his fourth 300-yard effort of the season, but the yardage came on a season-high number of pass attempts and season-low completion percentage. The Giants' notoriously stingy pass defense frequently stymied the Jaguars' typically efficient air attack, and Lawrence threw multiple interceptions for the first time this season. Lawrence did have what seemed to be a second-half touchdown pass to Parker Washington in the back of the end zone ruled incomplete and surprisingly confirmed as such on replay, but the 2021 first overall pick will be looking to get back to his mistake-free ways in a favorable Week 12 home matchup with a Titans team he threw for a season-high 352 yards against in Week 10.

injuries.longComment: Jeanty's 169 yards from scrimmage amounted to the second-highest single-game total of his career after going for 188 such yards against the Texans in Week 16 of last season. His performance was fueled by a 68-yard catch and run for a touchdown and a 46-yard rush, the latter of which marked his first of 20-plus yards on the campaign. Jeanty also broke a streak of four straight contests falling short of 10 carries, but considering No. 2 RB Mike Washington also earned nine runs in Week 11, the Raiders backfield remains a committee ahead of next Sunday's outing at Cleveland.

Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. injuries.longComment: With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants' offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production moving forward.

injuries.longComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid," adding, "but we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." Back on Nov. 22, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable would suggests that in a best case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team could consider Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative option, but Vrabel has indicated that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

injuries.longComment: Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. injuries.longComment: McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

injuries.longComment: Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

injuries.longComment: Metcalf was disqualified with 4:53 remaining in the third quarter Sunday after he attempted to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. He was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct in what was his second major transgression of the game; Metcalf previously drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the first half, when he held his block of DeJean well after a play had finished. Though Metcalf won't miss further game action as a result of his ejection, he may have already lost the faith of his fantasy managers heading into a Week 12 matchup with the Broncos on Friday. Metcalf has hauled in just 36 of his 74 targets (48.6 percent catch rate) and has scored just two touchdowns on the season while topping 60 receiving yards in only two of his 10 appearances.

injuries.longComment: Rodgers threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Max Hurleman on Pittsburgh's final offensive play with 1:21 remaining in the fourth quarter, but that was too little too late, as the Eagles proceeded to run out the clock to drop the Steelers to 6-4. Hurleman stepped up down the stretch in his first NFL game after starting wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified. Rodgers had a four-game stretch in which he threw 11 touchdown passes while posting at least 235 passing yards in each outing, but he has failed to reach that yardage total in any of his last four starts while recording only four TDs during the latter stretch. Snapping out of this recent funk won't be easy for Rodgers against the stout Broncos defense Friday.

injuries.longComment: San Francisco officially has parted ways with Aiyuk, whose two-week roster exemption expired Monday after he filed his paperwork for reinstatement. Given that Aiyuk has approximately $58 million in non-guaranteed money remaining on his contract and hasn't even practiced in a professional setting since sustaining a multi-ligament right knee tear in October 2024, he'll almost certainly go unclaimed off waivers and become a free agent. Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, recently said that the 28-year-old is considered fully healthy, and he's expected to work out for interested teams once he clears waivers. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relays that landing with the Commanders as a member of their practice squad is viewed as "the most likely option" for Aiyuk.

items.text: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps were also third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

injuries.longComment: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.
injuries.shortComment: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuries.longComment: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.
injuries.shortComment: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.

injuries.longComment: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuries.shortComment: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuries.longComment: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.
injuries.shortComment: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuries.longComment: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

injuries.longComment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuries.shortComment: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuries.longComment: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.
injuries.shortComment: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
